question: Catalyst Definition
content: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy. Crucially, the catalyst itself is not consumed by the reaction.
description: Your team is struggling to adopt a new project management tool. A senior developer builds a simple migration script that converts all old data into the new format automatically. Adoption skyrockets. What role did the developer play?
options: The developer was the project manager for the migration initiative
The developer acted as a catalyst — the migration script lowered the activation energy of adoption without being consumed by the process
The developer should have been building product features instead of tooling scripts
The migration script reduced the quality of the data transfer
answer: The developer acted as a catalyst — the migration script lowered the activation energy of adoption without being consumed by the process
explanation: The migration script is the catalyst. It lowers the barrier to adoption (eliminating manual data entry) and is not consumed — it can be reused for future migrations. After adoption, the script remains unchanged. The team crossed the activation barrier more easily because of this catalyst.

question: Catalysts Are Not Consumed
content: The defining characteristic of a catalyst is that it is not consumed or permanently altered by the reaction. After the reaction, the catalyst can be recovered and reused.
description: A consultant designs a new operating model for a company, trains the leadership team, and leaves. Two years later, the operating model is still running successfully. How does this illustrate catalysis?
options: The consultant was overpaid for a relatively simple deliverable
The consultant acted as a catalyst — she introduced a framework that lowered the activation energy for better operations, and was not consumed (she left the system unchanged)
The company would have adopted the operating model even without the consultant
The consultant should have stayed longer to ensure continued success
answer: The consultant acted as a catalyst — she introduced a framework that lowered the activation energy for better operations, and was not consumed (she left the system unchanged)
explanation: The consultant functioned as a true catalyst: she provided an alternative pathway (the new operating model) that lowered the barrier to better performance, and she was not consumed by the process — she left the organization intact. The new model became self-sustaining.

question: Finding the Catalyst
content: When facing a massive change effort that requires too much activation energy, ask: What element can I introduce to the environment that lowers the barrier without being consumed?
description: A company wants all employees to use a new internal knowledge base, but adoption is slow because contributing content feels like extra work. What would be an effective catalyst?
options: Require knowledge base contributions in everyone's performance review
Hire a dedicated team to write all the content themselves
Introduce a template system and a browser extension that makes adding content as easy as clicking a button — lowering the contribution barrier without being consumed
Send a weekly email reminding people to contribute to the knowledge base
answer: Introduce a template system and a browser extension that makes adding content as easy as clicking a button — lowering the contribution barrier without being consumed
explanation: A template system and browser extension are catalysts. They lower the energy required to contribute (no more formatting, no more navigating to the right page) without being consumed — they remain available for everyone to use repeatedly. The barrier drops, adoption rises.

question: Catalysts vs Raw Force
content: Brute-forcing a bottleneck through willpower, cash, or pressure is exhausting and resource-intensive. Introducing a catalyst is almost always more efficient because it permanently lowers the barrier.
description: A law firm wants partners to submit timesheets daily instead of weekly. The managing partner threatens to withhold bonuses for late submissions. Compliance improves marginally but partners are resentful. What approach does the catalyst model suggest instead?
options: Increase the penalty until compliance reaches 100%
Fire the partners who refuse to comply with the new policy
Find the friction causing late submissions and build a catalyst — perhaps a simple mobile app or email-based reminder that makes daily submission effortless
Accept weekly submissions since the policy change was not worth the conflict
answer: Find the friction causing late submissions and build a catalyst — perhaps a simple mobile app or email-based reminder that makes daily submission effortless
explanation: Threats are raw force — they consume management energy and generate resentment. A catalyst (like a simple submission tool) permanently lowers the barrier to compliance without ongoing force. Once introduced, the catalyst continues working without consuming additional energy.

question: Systemic Catalysts
content: The most powerful catalysts are systemic — they exist in the environment and lower barriers for everyone simultaneously, rather than requiring individual effort.
description: Stripe publishes standardized API documentation for online payments. Thousands of businesses build payment flows faster as a result. Stripe is not consumed by these integrations. What role does the API documentation play?
options: It is a marketing tool to attract more customers to Stripe
It acts as a systemic catalyst — it lowers the activation energy for online payment integration for every business that uses it, without being consumed
API documentation is a legal requirement for payment processors
It is a competitive advantage that only benefits Stripe's enterprise clients
answer: It acts as a systemic catalyst — it lowers the activation energy for online payment integration for every business that uses it, without being consumed
explanation: Well-designed API documentation is a systemic catalyst. It exists in the environment and lowers the barrier to payment integration for all developers. Stripe recovers no energy from the reaction — the catalyst remains unchanged. This is why platform companies invest heavily in developer experience.

question: The Catalyst Question
content: Whenever you face a persistent problem that requires ongoing force to solve, ask: What catalyst could permanently reduce the need for force?
description: A product team constantly interrupts the engineering team with urgent requests, destroying productivity. The engineering manager tries saying 'no' more often, but the interruptions continue. What catalyst should she look for?
options: Install a strict ticketing system with a three-day SLA for all requests
Hold a meeting to explain why interruptions are harmful to productivity
Find a systemic catalyst — perhaps a self-service tool that lets product run common experiments without engineering involvement, permanently removing the need for interruptions
Escalate the issue to the VP of Engineering to enforce better boundaries
answer: Find a systemic catalyst — perhaps a self-service tool that lets product run common experiments without engineering involvement, permanently removing the need for interruptions
explanation: Saying 'no' is brute force that must be reapplied constantly. A self-service tool is a catalyst — it lowers the barrier for product to get what they need without engineering involvement, and it is not consumed. The tool solves the problem permanently rather than requiring ongoing force.

question: Social Catalysts
content: Certain individuals function as social catalysts — their presence, credibility, or enthusiasm lowers the activation energy for group action or consensus.
description: A cross-functional team has been deadlocked on a strategic decision for weeks. A respected senior leader who has no direct stake in the outcome joins one meeting, asks three questions, and the team reaches consensus within an hour. What happened?
options: The senior leader forced the team to agree by exercising authority
The senior leader acted as a social catalyst — their neutral credibility and framing questions lowered the barrier to consensus without being consumed by the decision
The team was ready to agree and just needed any external input
The senior leader made the decision for the team
answer: The senior leader acted as a social catalyst — their neutral credibility and framing questions lowered the barrier to consensus without being consumed by the decision
explanation: Some people are social catalysts. Their mere presence lowers the activation energy for alignment — they ask the right questions, reduce political risk, and provide psychological safety. Like chemical catalysts, they enable the reaction without being changed by it.

question: Self-Reinforcing Catalysts
content: Some catalysts create conditions that further lower the activation energy over time, making the reaction progressively easier rather than staying constant.
description: A company adopts a new communication platform. As more people join, the platform becomes more valuable (network effects). Each new user lowers the barrier for the next user to join. How does this differ from a standard catalyst?
options: Network effects are not related to catalysis because they are a social phenomenon
This is a self-reinforcing catalyst — the catalyst's own presence lowers the barrier further over time, unlike standard catalysts which have a constant effect
Standard catalysts also self-reinforce in chemical reactions
Network effects always lead to a single platform dominating the market
answer: This is a self-reinforcing catalyst — the catalyst's own presence lowers the barrier further over time, unlike standard catalysts which have a constant effect
explanation: Most catalysts provide a constant rate enhancement. But some catalysts are self-reinforcing: each use of the catalyst makes it more effective. In network effects, each new user adds value that attracts more users, progressively lowering the adoption barrier. This creates powerful flywheels.
